decisions.statement: The pages written are the pages the index names of that page type.
A page type with no property under the key is refused.
A key its page type says carries many values is refused.
A page type no page is of is refused rather than answered as no edit.
A value that parses as no value is refused.
The value is written as the caller spells it rather than as text to quote.
The key is put in where the pages of that page type write that key.
An `after` the caller states places the key on every page.
A page the index files no value for gains the key last.
One page refused refuses the whole change.
A refusal over a page names that page.
The edits are worked out by the change reached.
That change acts on a page type, as this one does.
That change is reached through the runner rather than by an import.
Nothing here works out a body of its own.
Nothing here reads a page's own body.

definition: one value put under one key on every page of one page type
